title: Two engineers edited the same function

scenario.brief:
Two changes to `applyDiscount` in `src/pricing.js` landed on different branches this week:

- On `main`, Jonas made discounted totals round to cents so invoices stop showing values like `41.3299999`.
- On `fix/discount-cap`, Mei fixed a policy bug: discounts above 50% were being honoured. Her change clamps the rate with `Math.min(discount, MAX_DISCOUNT)`.

Both changes are correct and both must survive. Merge `fix/discount-cap` into `main`. Git will stop with a conflict because both branches edited the same lines of the same function.

Resolve it so the final `applyDiscount` clamps the rate **and** rounds the result, remove every conflict marker, stage the file and complete the merge. The tests in `test/pricing.test.js` describe the expected behaviour if you want to check your resolution by reading.
scenario.whyItMatters: Conflicts are not errors; they are Git asking a human to make a decision it cannot make safely. Engineers who resolve conflicts calmly and correctly, keeping both intents, are the ones trusted to integrate other people's work.

files.README.md:
# Billing Service

Computes invoice totals, discounts and taxes for Brightwater Energy customers.

steps.author: mei
steps.message:
Clamp discount rate at MAX_DISCOUNT

A promo code with a 90% discount was honoured in full. Policy caps
discounts at 50% of the subtotal.

steps.author: jonas
steps.message:
Round discounted totals to cents

Floating point error produced totals like 41.3299999 on invoices.
steps.label: main-tip

objectives.title: Start merging fix/discount-cap into main and hit the conflict
hints: Make sure you are on main, then merge the fix branch. The conflict is expected.
`git merge fix/discount-cap` will report CONFLICT (content) in src/pricing.js and leave markers in the file. `git status` lists it under Unmerged paths.
Run `git merge fix/discount-cap`, then open src/pricing.js (`code src/pricing.js`) to see both versions between the markers.

objectives.title: Make applyDiscount clamp the rate and round the result
objectives.description: Both Math.min(discount, MAX_DISCOUNT) and Math.round(...) must be present in the committed file.
hints: Everything between `<<<<<<< HEAD` and `=======` is main's version; between `=======` and `>>>>>>> fix/discount-cap` is Mei's. You need a function that does both.
A correct body: compute `const rate = Math.min(discount, MAX_DISCOUNT)`, then `const discounted = total - total * rate`, then `return Math.round(discounted * 100) / 100`.
In the editor use Accept Both and then edit so the three lines above appear once, in order. Remove any leftover duplicate return.

objectives.title: Remove every conflict marker and stage the resolution
hints: Conflict markers are plain text; if you commit them the code will not even parse.
After editing, `git add src/pricing.js` tells Git the conflict is resolved. `git diff` should show no `<<<<<<<` lines.
Run `git add src/pricing.js`, then `git status` should say "All conflicts fixed but you are still merging".

objectives.title: Complete the merge with a merge commit on main
hints: A merge that stopped for conflicts is finished by committing.
`git commit` with no message opens the editor with the prepared merge message; `-m` works too.
Run `git commit` (or `git merge --continue`) and check `git log --oneline --graph` for the two-parent commit.

debrief.summary: You merged two conflicting edits to the same function, preserved both intents, and recorded the result as a merge commit.
internals: Git found the merge base (the scaffold commit) and diffed both branches against it. Both diffs touched the same lines in applyDiscount, so the three-way merge could not pick a side.
Git wrote the conflicted file with markers and recorded the path as unmerged. The merge paused with `MERGE_HEAD` pointing at fix/discount-cap so `git commit` knows to create a two-parent commit.
`git add` replaced the unmerged entry with your resolved blob. The merge commit's tree contains that blob; its parents are the previous main tip and the fix branch tip.
Only the conflicted file needed attention. Files changed on one side only were merged automatically.

keyCommands.note: Starts the merge; stops on conflicts.
Lists unmerged paths and tells you how to continue or abort.
During a conflict, shows the conflicted regions.
Give up and return to the pre-merge state. Always available.
Take one whole side when that is the right answer.

commonMistakes: Taking one side wholesale ("accept current") and silently dropping the other engineer's fix.
Leaving a marker line behind; the file no longer parses and CI fails.
Forgetting `git add` after editing and wondering why `git commit` refuses.
Panicking and deleting the repository. `git merge --abort` restores the pre-merge state in one command.
debrief.atWork: Conflicts appear whenever two people touch the same area, which is constant on active teams. Resolving them is a communication task as much as a technical one: when the right combination is unclear, ask the other author rather than guessing.
debrief.interview: "Walk me through resolving a merge conflict." Mention reading both sides, understanding intent, editing to a correct combination, removing markers, `git add`, then committing, and knowing `--abort` exists.

solution: git commit -m "Merge branch 'fix/discount-cap'" -m "Keep both the discount cap and cent rounding in applyDiscount."
